Charlie (support): Escalation from a customer hitting /v1/rerank — getting 400 with 'invalid items'. Customer attached the payload they sent and the API response. Can someone triage?

Maria (eng-runtime): Can you paste the exact request body and the raw 400 response? quick check: often this is candidates typed as a string or topk as a string.

Charlie (support): Here's the curl they sent (redacted token):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"items":[{"id":"abc123","query":"best widget","candidates":"a,b,c"}], "TopK":"3"}'
```
Server returned: `400 Bad Request` and body: `{\"error\":\"invalid items: candidates must be an array\"}`

Raj (oncall): Yep, that payload will trip strict schema validation. Two things: 1) candidates must be an array of objects/strings, not a CSV string; 2) topk/TopK must be an integer field named `top_k` or `topK` (our docs say `topK` camelCase), but sending it as a string will fail type checks.

support-bot: Automated note: 400 -> MISSING_OR_INVALID_FIELD. Field: `items[0].candidates` (expected array).

Maria (eng-runtime): Thanks, reproducer is simple. Quick repro curl that fails the same way so eng can write a failing test:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"items":[{"id":"abc123","query":"best widget","candidates":"a,b,c"}], "TopK":3}'
```
Notice TopK numeric but wrong key casing + candidates string. Both cause validation errors.

Charlie (support): Customer says this worked on their old client code — they were massaging the body before sending and a regression in their SDK removed that step. They've reverted but asked if we can give a clearer error message so the next engineer sees exactly which field and expected type.

Maria (eng-runtime): Agree. Action items: 1) I'll add a more explicit validation error message: e.g. `items[0].candidates: expected array of candidate objects/strings, got string`. 2) Add a unit test in runtime validation for mis-cased keys and CSV candidates. 3) Doc note in support FAQ showing common bad payload examples and a corrected sample. Assigning to me, will PR today.

Raj (oncall): If you can, also return an example of corrected payload in the error body (small JSON snippet) — that'll reduce back-and-forth.

Charlie (support): Perfect. I'll reply to the customer with the corrected payload and a short explanation of the two issues. Sample corrected body to send them: 
```json
{"items":[{"id":"abc123","query":"best widget","candidates":["a","b","c"]}],"topK":3}
```

support-bot: Ticket #INC-4129 updated: assigned -> Maria (eng-runtime). ETA: today for PR, docs update in next sprint.

Maria (eng-runtime): Thanks. I'll link the PR here when ready.

Charlie (support): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
